title: Who draws the line?
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: If you had to draw a line on what may be said, who would you let draw it?
Jose took a vote on censorship or no censorship and asked each person for a short reason. One student said: I am in the middle. Having some censorship is good, but I know the effects can be bad.
Jose asked: who should decide? A student answered: it should be some sort of council or committee, with guidelines and several people voting, not one individual.

Jose said that this is where it gets difficult: the responsibility of saying, I am going to censor people, so I will pick five people to do it. You are almost playing God. Where is the line? Somebody has to come up with a line.
Another student voted for none: when people see things that are unacceptable it is evident, so people make their own decisions.

Jose said he was asking everyone to vote because he wanted to see where each person stands, and he gave his own line as: be disciplined about not judging, and about listening, despite what the person says.
Where is your own line, and who would you trust to hold it with you?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a question where you are in the middle.
Write who should decide it, and why.
Write what could go wrong with one decider.
Write what could go wrong with a committee.
Write your own line in one sentence.

check.q: What did Jose ask everyone to give with their vote?
What did one student say should decide, not one individual?
What did Jose say a decider is almost doing?

recap: A hard line needs a decider. Say who, and own your own line.
